semantics: These are binding scenario requirements, not a self-executing universal runner. Applicability is conjunctive per conformance unit, never a Cartesian product of a global manifest: unit capabilities cover capabilities, the unit declares every requires_profiles value and the vector layer, and it declares none of excludes_capabilities, excludes_profiles, or excludes_layers; an absent requires_profiles/excludes selector is universal for the remaining capability and layer predicate. An exclusion is a factual negative selector whose absence must also be proved by runtime trace for every unit target; manifest omission alone is not evidence. That makes the vector a candidate: any unmapped target or result path is a failure, never a reason for non-applicability. Every unit is an independent target-scoped conformance scope; no capability, profile, layer, target, or limit is inherited or unioned across units. Adapters sharing any state-domain identity (bytes, cache, security context, subscription, journal, command, or rollout) MUST be consolidated into one owner unit with all factual targets, capabilities, profiles, and layers. Every state-domain identity is referenced by exactly one unit; an additional relationship unit, relation/composition unit, or reuse of that domain is forbidden. Mixed public/protected or mixed auth-mode ownership of one state domain is NO-GO; stateless code or infrastructure alone does not create a state domain. Every unit includes each factual profile and exposed layer. Each harness maps every named target and result path to a documented HTTP, SSE, cache, database, and worker adapter; a synthesized assertion also fails the vector. One unit execution writes the single unit-level result_document and trace_evidence; assertions and $result_ref never read another unit. Every {$limit_ref:name,delta:n} resolves to unit.limits[name]+n, must remain a nonnegative interoperable integer, and configures the real adapter before the scenario. requires_limits is exactly the set of refs in that vector. The result document records the unmodified unit limits under /effective_limits and trace evidence proves the applied configuration; testing a substitute threshold fails. Every required limit has exactly one boundary_probe in its vector. A boundary probe runs two fresh, isolated real-adapter cases with every other dimension strictly below its bound: a valid workload at N must be accepted and observed at N, while the same workload at N+1 must be rejected specifically by the named limiter. It writes effective_limit, at_limit_accepted, at_limit_observed, over_limit_rejected, and rejection_reason under /limit_boundaries/{limit}; those five values are implicit mandatory assertions. Reject-all, a smaller hidden threshold, or rejection by another dimension fails. retry_after_ms is serialized by the harness as an HTTP Retry-After value no earlier than that duration, or as the equivalent SSE retry field for a native stream. Actions execute in array order except consecutive concurrent_write actions with the same concurrency_group: every actor reaches a prepare barrier, the harness releases them together, and the trace must prove overlap. In an action body, an object whose only member is $result_ref dereferences that prior RFC 6901 result path. absent/present do not take a value, one_of takes an array, unchanged compares with given, absent_or_lte passes when the path is absent or its value is at most the given value, contains_token parses a comma-delimited HTTP field case-insensitively and matches a complete trimmed token/directive name (before any equals value) rather than a substring, lt and the other ordering operators compare resolved numeric values, and an assertion string value beginning with @ dereferences that RFC 6901 result path before comparison; all other operators compare value directly.  Structural JSON Schema validation alone is not an execution pass. Redirect handling is target-scoped: snapshot/repair, fetch-stream, and lease may follow only 307/308 to a configured allowlisted origin, at most one hop, with no-store, full destination reauthorization, and no ambient cross-origin credential forwarding unless explicitly scoped; command issuance/submit/lookup and native EventSource follow no 3xx and retry only their configured local endpoint. Rollout fault injection is likewise target-scoped: absent repair, replay, realtime, protected, patch, or command facets are proved absent with zero numerator and trace evidence and are never synthesized.

vectors.description: An ETag learned by principal A cannot probe or obtain A's snapshot as principal B.
A valid stream/version tuple does not authorize repair in another tenant.
Principal B cannot look up A's receipt with a copied receipt token.
A resume token copied across tenant or subscription cannot select another journal.
A credentialless public cache endpoint rejects Cookie, Authorization, and bearer query credentials independently rather than varying secretly by any of them.
A public response is credentialless, cookie-free, variant-safe, and byte-stable for its cursor.
Private snapshot, repair, and authentication errors each prohibit HTTP/CDN storage.
A protected replay response is private and never stored.
A protected SSE response is private, non-storable, and non-transformable.
A protected command receipt is private and never stored.
A protected Continuum response cannot be inserted into Cache API by application code.
Two rollout profiles or schemas cannot share a public representation key.
A client advertising only N-1 receives N-1 and a cache-visible negotiated variant.
After observing head 20, a lagging replica cannot freshen installed head 10 with 304 or 200.
Origin semantic age, subsequent HTTP cache age, and local request/parse time are successive intervals and all add.
A mutation between snapshot and subscribe is replayed strictly after the atomic delivery cursor.
Independent snapshot cursors for A and B cannot be concatenated into a multiplex resume token by the client.
A ready head detects a cached snapshot older than a mutation committed before registration, even with no later event.
Protected SSE is rejected at configuration when status/lease revocation cannot be observed.

Cookie-authenticated protected native EventSource obtains a CSRF-protected canonical lease, establishes an owner-scoped ready cut, rejects single-axis BOLA attempts, and expires without restarting the original deadline.

Two distinct initial lease operations in one cookie session receive independent subscription routes; each native route must match its full context and security generation, while swapped, foreign-session, and revoked ids fail identically before journal access or bytes.
A mutation racing subscription registration is queued behind the atomic ready barrier and cannot arrive first.
A logged-in same-origin page cannot silently send session cookies to a public native EventSource endpoint.
Replay and an exact caught-up head remain stale until canonical HTTP validation.
Protected replay and an exact caught-up head remain stale until an authorized canonical HTTP validation.
A caught-up checkpoint ahead of installed state proves a gap, not freshness.
A protected caught-up checkpoint ahead of installed state proves a gap, not freshness.
Original and re-enveloped replay copies with identical data collapse before same-base fork detection.
A replay base equal to the retention floor is repairable, while the immediately preceding base gets an explicit reset.
Repair 10 to 11 installs first, then the buffered exact-base 11 to 12 patch drains once.
If the browser saved an SSE id before reducer dispatch, a reconnect checkpoint still carries a future head and starts repair even without replay capability.
A protected reconnect checkpoint retains a future head when dispatch was interrupted and starts authorized repair.
A mutation committed during replay-to-live handoff is covered by the caught-up cut or delivered live exactly once.
A multiplexed checkpoint that omits B or duplicates A cannot close replay for an A+B manifest.
A caught-up callback queued by connection A cannot affect connection B after reconnect.
A protected caught-up callback queued by connection A cannot affect connection B after reconnect.
A queued caught-up control processed after hard expiry stays blocked until canonical HTTP validation.
A queued protected caught-up control processed after hard expiry remains blocked until authorized canonical HTTP validation.
Exactly one event beyond the declared queue limit disconnects/resets without unbounded growth.
A suspended consumer cannot receive more events than the subscription-generation budget before forced repair.
Producer or proxy rejects a line above max_sse_line_bytes before native EventSource materializes it.
A reauthorization control is processed after a newer data head instead of being discarded as a data regression.
When reauthorization wins first, a queued event from the previous security generation is discarded.

The SSE `continuum-security-generation` exception is ordered and deduplicated only in the current subscription's security domain: lower renew, duplicate renew, foreign-subscription control, and renew after terminal purge cannot extend or resurrect a lease or advance projection state.
Malformed, duplicate-key, oversized, too-deep, too-wide, oversized-result, and dangerous-key JSON never mutates installed state.
A gap/repair in stream A does not block or contaminate ordered updates in stream B on the same connection.
A unique/CAS constraint permits only one writer to allocate a stream epoch sequence.
Crash after commit cannot make a committed projection version undiscoverable: outbox/CDC may publish it, or canonical reconciliation must observe it.
Crash before the database transaction commits exposes neither view/version nor outbox event.
A rebuild begun at revision 10 loses CAS when incremental processing has already installed 11.
A failover without a durable counter rotates epoch under a new fence, and the partitioned old writer cannot commit or publish.
Restoring older storage creates a new epoch and cannot emit into the historical generation.
The durable authority fence makes a partitioned old replica fail closed with 503; redirect behavior is exercised separately so this case cannot pass by choosing the easier branch.
A repeated client digest with changed normalized request body conflicts and never duplicates the effect.

Equal, later, lower, and contradictory local versions follow the closed fence rules; a local epoch mismatch requires canonical receipt lookup, a higher authorized receipt revision may replace the fence across a legitimate epoch, an older revision cannot undo it, and later reuse of the abandoned epoch is invalid.
Repeating command-id issuance with the same nonce returns the same scoped id and performs no business effect.
A server-issued command id is rejected outside its authenticated principal and operation scope.
Two concurrent first uses of one command id with different intents permit one CAS winner and no duplicate effect.
Disabling a rollout profile ends streams, drops buffers, and forces canonical fetch under the baseline profile.
Known and minimum semantic versions are each all-or-none tuples; a partial tuple is rejected before any projection read.
Public cache directives are bounded by semantic freshness, and 304 repeats the complete boundary rather than inheriting looser metadata.
Both a successful stream and an authorization error carry the non-store/no-transform boundary.
A ready/caught-up frame whose SSE id differs from its JSON delivery cursor cannot choose either resume position.
A protected ready/caught-up frame whose SSE id differs from its JSON delivery cursor cannot choose either resume position.
An authenticated initial grant creates subscription and security generation atomically without requiring impossible prior ids.
Server-reported lease age plus network, parse, and suspended-tab delay are subtracted from lease_for_ms; a fully consumed grant installs nothing.
A protected callback started under a security generation and authorization fence cannot parse or reinstall data after lease expiry increments the fence and purges protected state.
Even when a purge frame is lost, revocation closes the open connection, local expiry purges state, and reconnect without a new grant is denied.
A stream reauthorize revokes the old generation and only the later canonical grant activates the pending generation.
Splitting one event across individually valid data lines cannot exceed max_sse_event_data_bytes after concatenation.
Raw, parsed, installed, worker-copy, multi-stream, and new-generation allocations share one quota that a reconnect cannot reset.
Compressed size, decoded size, expansion ratio, and decompression time are each bounded before JSON materialization.

Public SSR is safe before hydration only when a CSP-authorized parser-blocking no-import guard runs before any fresh/current claim, or the document is born stale_usable; navigate-away and bfcache restore after hard expiry never restart embedded freshness, although useful public content may remain visible.
A public snapshot intercepted by a service worker bypasses Cache API so service-worker-served offline reloads cannot freeze Age and extend its hard expiry; normal HTTP caching remains allowed.
A rebuild pinned at source watermark 10 cannot read a domain mutation at 11 and label those bytes as projection cursor 10.
The submit horizon can expire while an accepted command remains durable and lookupable until a terminal receipt.
Kill switch during candidate repair protects an N-1 bfcache tab and service worker from candidate bytes and converges through the baseline endpoint.
A valid grant for another subscription manifest cannot activate a generation or subscription.
Retrying one logical lease operation with a new transport correlation id returns the same grant and cannot create two active generations.

Lease idempotency is keyed by full authorized context plus manifest and operation id: same-op retries return one grant, cross-axis reuse never returns it, distinct initial ops in one session may form independent lineages, and context revocation invalidates all lineages.

The successor CAS slot is the lineage root plus previous subscription/generation and pending generation, independent of operation id: one authorized context and manifest fingerprint wins, an equivalent request repeats that winner, and a different-manifest competitor conflicts without forking or purging the winner.

Renew is an N-to-N+1 CAS in the same security generation: same-operation retries and different-operation requests with an equivalent fingerprint reproduce one winner, while a divergent fingerprint receives 409 and cannot revoke or purge the current winning generation.

Malformed manifest digests and duplicate ids fail at syntax validation, while canonical unknown or known-but-unauthorized ids reach per-id authorization and fail non-enumeratingly without partial lease state.
Repeating an issuance nonce after a lost response returns the same command id with nondecreasing issuance age and preserves the original retry horizon.

A document containing a Continuum bootstrap and intercepted by a service worker bypasses service-worker storage so a service-worker-served offline reload cannot restart its semantic age; normal HTTP caching remains allowed.
A crash after local commit leaves a durable outbox, and redelivery uses the command idempotency key so the provider and local receipt converge to one proven effect.
If an external response is lost and no durable lookup proves the result, the command reaches terminal indeterminate within its SLA and is never reported committed.
An indefinite fetch-stream uses identity content encoding, counts multiline event data cumulatively, and cancels before an oversized event reaches JSON parsing.
A protected fetch-stream distinguishes HTTP denial from network failure, cancels the reader, and purges without treating either as a live authorized stream.
A public fetch-stream explicitly omits browser credentials and never relies on Cookie or Authorization variation.
A fetch-stream observes Retry-After, local backoff bounds, and single-flight reconnection rather than starting a reconnect storm.
An old strong ETag cannot produce 304 after the authoritative semantic tuple changes, even when domain JSON happens to be byte-identical.
The harness perturbs every deployment-declared byte-affecting public dimension, alone and in combination, and proves distinct bytes never collide while query ordering normalizes.
Every successful SSE response, public or protected, prevents storage and transformation by browsers, proxies, and CDNs.

Continuum-Age-Ms is age since the latest authoritative validation cut. The first 200 serialized at that cut equals the byte-stable body age; a later canonical 200 or authorized 304 for the exact current tuple may create a new cut and reset the header while the body and ETag remain byte-stable. Effective age is Continuum-Age-Ms plus HTTP Age plus local elapsed, never max(body, header).
Retrying one lost renewal with a stable lease operation id returns the same revision, echoes each attempt, and cannot move the renewal deadline.
Wrong or missing attempt correlation, missing lease age, and a decreasing age on retry all fail closed without installing authorization.

A 128-bit client issuance nonce is idempotent only inside authority, environment, tenant, principal, and operation; the same bytes in another authorized scope or operation allocate an independent command id without querying or disclosing the original scope.
The immutable retry horizon returned when a command id is issued is the same horizon carried by accepted and terminal receipts.
Repair remains single-flight and stops at the unit's declared attempt and elapsed retry limits.
Streams, concurrent connections, event rate, reconnect rate, and canonical reconciliation use the unit's declared bounds.
The bounded message-id dedupe index evicts at N+1 without weakening cursor, token, and digest equivocation checks.
A JSON Patch with N+1 operations is rejected before any operation or candidate result is applied.
Replay exceeding its event, byte, or elapsed window terminates with reset rather than a truncated successful suffix.
Native EventSource retry instructions cannot delay or accelerate reconnect beyond the local backoff bound and single-flight gate.
Command and receipt payloads enforce compressed, decoded, shape, result, resident, ratio, and time limits before installation.

Every initial or resumed physical SSE connection has a new transport generation and sends continuum-ready as its first non-heartbeat control; losing the first ready callback after the user agent advanced Last-Event-ID cannot cause a loop because reconnect establishes a new ready and caught_up is accepted only from that same connection.

Native EventSource sends no custom Accept parameters; a trusted local URI selects protocol major, manifest, and schema, ready is the first non-heartbeat echo before data, mismatches close, and N and N-1 endpoints coexist.

A public native subscription generation is carried by the opaque Last-Event-ID cursor and its event/byte/time budgets are cumulative across reconnects; exhaustion returns 204, suppresses EventSource recreation until the next top-level navigation, and keeps correctness through canonical polling without allowing isolated fetch or rotated cursors to reopen SSE.

Decoded response status/pseudoheaders plus headers are bounded before cache, service worker, or application processing on every status; N is accepted and N+1, including a huge ETag/state-token on 304, aborts without parsing a truncated field or renewing freshness.

Command-id, submit, receipt, auth-lease, conditional 304, and error response heads share the same decoded head bound before cache/SW/client state; N+1 aborts with no receipt, lease, or effect installation.

Finite snapshot and repair requests accept an exact N-byte request target/header set and selector, while N+1 is rejected as 414/431 by the named pre-authorization limiter with bounded reserved memory and zero lookup.

A protected lease POST accepts identity-encoded request JSON and an untrusted operation id at N, rejects N+1 body or identifier before auth/CAS, and rejects a tiny compressed carrier claiming a 100 MB nonce with 415 before decompression.

Command issuance, submit, retry, and lookup accept exact inbound head/body/identifier bounds and reject N+1 or non-identity content encoding before auth, nonce/idempotency/receipt lookup, allocation, fingerprint, or effect.

The rolling server-side command-operation limit counts issuance, submit/retry, and receipt lookup including idempotent repeats, independently per principal, tenant, and IP; nonce, command id, receipt token, operation, and auth identity rotation cannot reset it, and N+1 is rejected before lookup, allocation, effect, or existence disclosure.

Pending count, issuance retry, accepted-to-terminal, and terminal-relative receipt retention are independent exact bounds: accepted may first appear near the retry horizon, the first durable terminal revision starts the full retention window, and later fence revisions do not restart it.

Protected data lease lineage and operation-rate limits use the authenticated context: N distinct active roots and N attempts are accepted, duplicate or successor operations consume no extra root, disconnect and identifier rotation do not reset either bound, and N+1 is rejected by the named limiter before lease CAS lookup.
Command-only protected lease endpoints exercise the same active-lineage and authenticated attempt-rate boundaries without requiring a snapshot capability.
A protected data lease cannot exceed the unit bound and revocation closes and purges within its declared SLA.
Protected command issuance, submit, and receipt lookup cannot outlive the unit lease or revocation SLA.

A command-only client activates grants only for exact recomputed manifests whose every id is authorized; malformed inputs fail 400, while canonical unknown or unauthorized ids fail indistinguishably with no partial generation.
Command lease grant and renewal retries keep stable operation identity, echo the current attempt, preserve revision/deadline, and reject missing, wrong, or decreasing age metadata.
A command-only client cannot extend or resurrect issuance, submit, or receipt authority with duplicate, lower, or post-purge lease revisions.
A command receipt callback captured before lease expiry cannot parse, install, retry, or publish after expiry advances the authorization fence.
Protected command issuance, submit, and receipt responses bypass Cache API and cannot be persisted by a service worker.
A subscribe-first multiplex becomes usable only after one ready barrier exactly covers the requested stream set, digest, and subscription identity.
A snapshot-first multiplex obtains all snapshots and one opaque vector cursor from the same atomic cut, then replays a mutation that happened after that cut.

A public snapshot-only rollout kill switch increments a generation fence so an in-flight candidate response, cached candidate bytes, and an N-1 bfcache callback cannot install after rollback; the baseline canonical snapshot restores convergence without fabricating realtime repair.

A command rollout kill switch fences pending issuance, submit, and receipt callbacks, keeps the baseline ledger receipt authoritative with the same command id/fingerprint, stores no command bytes in cache/SW, and never fabricates data repair or repeats the effect.
Every public snapshot explicitly chooses non-storable delivery or a complete shared-cache key; public classification alone never enables heuristic shared caching.
SSR bootstrap serialization escapes a closing-script payload, creates no attacker DOM or executable script, and is covered by an effective CSP.

A protected SSR target is conforming only with a CSP-nonced or hashed parser-blocking no-import guard in head before any protected markup/bootstrap; navigate-away before hydration synchronously purges, and an old-generation document cannot hydrate protected bytes.

A target-specific protected SSR guard runs before markup and synchronously fences and purges lease, state, buffers, validators, DOM, and bootstrap on the first hidden/pagehide/freeze signal; pageshow.persisted restores empty and blocks protected render until a new grant plus canonical fetch.
Command issuance, submit, and lookup use explicit HTTP semantics, private/no-store responses, validators, and stable correlation without treating a receipt token as authority.
The producer commits authoritative state, accepted receipt, and durable outbox in one transaction so crashes cannot orphan or duplicate a command effect.

Cookie-authenticated command issuance, submit, and auth-lease POSTs require an exact allowlisted Origin plus session-bound CSRF before allocation/effect, while safe receipt GET remains BOLA-authorized and mixed auth modes fail closed.
An accepted receipt remains lookupable and reaches a durable terminal or indeterminate status no later than the declared accepted-state deadline.
A neutral protected stream grants and subscribes for its owner, while cross-principal and cross-tenant probes create no lease, subscription, stream, or observable bytes.

An ordinary protected snapshot returns owner bytes, while one-axis principal, tenant, and second valid allowlisted authority mismatches are denied indistinguishably before projection, cache, ETag, or body access.

A protected SSR bootstrap serves the owner with private/no-store bytes, while principal, tenant, and second allowlisted authority mismatches are denied before projection/cache and expose neither ETag nor body.
A learned receipt locator, token, and ETag cannot turn cross-principal, cross-tenant, or second valid authority conditional lookup into a 304 or existence oracle; owner lookup alone may return 304.
Repair authority is independently bound to tenant, principal, normalized trusted authority, and operation before cache or projection access.
Replay cursors are independently bound to tenant, principal, trusted authority, subscription, and replay operation before journal access.

Command issuance nonces allocate independently after authorization in each scope, while an issued command id, submit, and receipt remain bound to tenant, principal, trusted authority, and operation before lookup or effect.
A merge-patch-only adapter validates duplicate, wrong and future bases, schema and digest mismatches, and dangerous keys before one atomic RFC 7396 application.
A merge-patch-only realtime adapter buffers an exact-next patch during repair, installs the repair base, then drains exactly once without requiring JSON Patch capability.

Snapshot-only promotion uses the declared comparison population and metric identifiers, fails closed below either sample floor, proves the absent realtime surface in trace, and reports reconnects as zero over operations without synthesizing a connection. Exact absent-facet comparator probes run only in the neutral evaluator.

Command-only promotion uses the command-operation population and named metrics, fails closed below either floor or without telemetry, proves data-repair and realtime surfaces absent, reports both rates as zero over command operations, and uses a pure neutral comparator for their exact threshold arithmetic without fabricating adapter events.
A cookie-authenticated protected snapshot accepts its trusted same-site origin but rejects credentialed cross-site CORS before projection or cache access.

A cookie-authenticated protected lease rejects cross-site, missing-CSRF, header-only, and ambiguous mixed-principal grant requests before auth lookup or subscription allocation; one same-origin session-bound CSRF request succeeds.
A protected non-cookie snapshot ignores cookies and query credentials, keeps credentialed CORS closed, and authorizes only the configured header or mTLS identity before BOLA checks.
A non-cookie protected lease rejects Cookie and query credentials before auth lookup and accepts only the configured Authorization header or mTLS identity with full BOLA reauthorization.
Non-cookie command endpoints reject cookie and query credentials before issuance, submit, or lookup, while configured header or mTLS identity remains subject to BOLA checks.
A public fetch-stream subscribe-first binding compares a schema-valid ready head with the cached snapshot and repairs a mutation committed before registration.
An authorized protected fetch-stream subscribe-first binding uses protected descriptors for ready and snapshot, then repairs the pre-registration mutation without crossing authority.
A protected multiplex accepts only a schema-valid ready control with its exact protected manifest, digest, subscription and unique stream descriptors.
A protected snapshot-first multiplex obtains protected snapshots and one vector cursor from the same authorized cut and replays the intervening mutation without losing it.

A protected snapshot-only kill switch advances rollout and authorization fences so late candidate, cached, N-1, and bfcache callbacks cannot parse, cache, or reinstall protected state; baseline reauthorization and canonical fetch restore convergence without synthetic realtime repair.
A protected merge-patch-only adapter accepts its exact authorized base and rejects duplicate, wrong/future base, schema, digest, and dangerous-key variants without partial protected state.
A protected merge-only realtime adapter buffers the protected next patch, installs the authorized repair base, and drains once under the same generation and fence.
A protected JSON Patch applies under the matching generation/fence, while a queued replay copy after reauthorization is discarded before parse or installation.

The snapshot runner attests each runtime-observed canonical backing identity and digest against the manifest; a possibly aliased resource whose disjointness cannot be proven fails closed instead of inventing evidence.
A command-only unit performs the same runtime canonical backing-identity attestation for command ledger, idempotency, outbox, and receipt state without relying on a snapshot vector.

For pure-local commands, precondition/domain-invariant evaluation, mutation, ledger, outbox, and terminal receipt share one transaction. For external commands, acceptance atomizes precondition plus reservation/local mutation, ledger, outbox, and accepted receipt; completion separately atomizes durable provider proof, final mutation or compensation, outbox state, and terminal receipt.

Operation schema and I-JSON/JCS validation precede fingerprinting; an out-of-range integer such as 9007199254740993 is rejected consistently across heterogeneous workers, and the hash covers exactly the single normalized object used by effect and outbox with no post-hash defaults or coercion.

Every command issuance/submit/precondition and protected lease JSON value recursively rejects __proto__, prototype, and constructor before normalization, fingerprinting, merge, authorization lookup, CAS, allocation, or effect unless represented in proven prototype-less maps.

On hide/freeze public data becomes at least stale_usable; wake/visibility/pageshow recomputes elapsed as the conservative maximum of nonnegative monotonic and wall deltas before any fresh claim, and an unproven or regressive interval blocks use until canonical validation.

Every protected browser, worker, or non-browser target uses a sleep-inclusive monotonic source or conservative elapsed interval; after a frozen hour or an ambiguous clock, the wake gate runs before parse/effect/paint, expires or invalidates the lease early, advances the fence, and purges. A runtime without that gate is NO-GO.

Representation freshness and protected lease anchors persist a fenced time-authority epoch plus nondecreasing elapsed lower/upper floors in the same CAS as the ETag/version or lease; restart, cold-cache failover, rollback, restore, and uncertainty never decrease age or make data fresh.

Issuance, retry, accepted, terminal-retention, and tombstone anchors persist a fenced time-authority epoch and monotone elapsed interval; upper bounds expire or deny early, lower bounds alone authorize GC, and uncertain accepted work becomes indeterminate without reopening terminal state.

A single durable command-ledger generation/fence is compared in the same linearizable commit as issuance, first bind, acceptance, completion, lookup, and GC. A split old primary or takeover without full ledger continuity cannot confirm, reissue, execute, expire, or collect old commands.

Canonical snapshot, repair, and failover may follow only a no-store 307 or 308 to one configured allowlisted origin; every other 3xx, an unallowlisted origin, a loop, or a second hop aborts before projection/cache reads. The destination reauthorizes the full scope and receives no ambient cross-origin credential unless explicitly scoped.

Fetch-stream follows only a no-store 307/308 one-hop redirect after validating the allowlisted destination, then reauthorizes the complete scope before reading any SSE byte; loops, second hops, other 3xx, and ambient credential forwarding fail closed.

A protected snapshot lease grant or renewal preserves POST semantics only across one allowlisted 307/308, reauthorizes full scope and CSRF at the destination, counts hop time in lease age, and never forwards ambient cross-origin credentials. All rejected redirects allocate no CAS, grant, lineage, subscription, or bytes.
The command-only protected lease endpoint obeys the same strict 307/308 one-hop redirect contract and cannot evade it by lacking snapshot capability.

Command issuance, submit, and receipt lookup plus native EventSource treat every 3xx as terminal failure and retry only the configured local endpoint; they never consume Location, forward credentials, or touch command/SSE state.
Native EventSource rejects every 3xx, including 307/308, closes before ready or data, and may reconnect only to its configured local protocol-major/manifest/schema URI.

A factual realtime unit executes target-scoped repair and reconnect faults, resets the window when population or metric identifiers change, fails closed on sample/telemetry gaps, and evaluates each of the seven thresholds at equality and the smallest representable value above it.

Public JSON Patch repair accepts a singleton or contiguous batch only when every patch has one stream/schema/epoch and response version/freshness headers describe the final patch target. Continuum-Age-Ms is anchored to the authoritative validation cut; isolated mismatches reject the whole response without install or freshness renewal. Every response echoes the current repair id and carries the strong ETag of the declared exact JCS UTF-8 response bytes; HTTP Age is seconds and is converted conservatively with the +999ms quantization ceiling before local elapsed.

vectors.description: Renewal final CAS captures the durable context authorization_epoch, active flag, lineage_policy_epoch, and current lease revision, then compares and commits them in the same serialization boundaries used by logout/revoke and purge/reauthorize. Both possible winners are exercised: transition-first blocks the old renewal; renew-first is immediately terminalized, so neither old nor newly returned lease crosses an authorization boundary or resurrects a lineage. Each ordering runs against separately provisioned durable state, and a controlled barrier pauses renewal after epoch capture but before final CAS so the raw trace proves the named winner rather than merely simultaneous request release.

vectors.description: Initial and successor grants recheck the durable authorization and lineage-policy epochs plus active status in their final CAS, at the same serialization boundary as logout/revoke and purge/reauthorize. Four independently provisioned cases force both total orders with controlled barriers: transition-first returns only the generic authorization denial and same-operation retry cannot replay a cached success; grant-first commits at most one lineage/successor and the following transition terminalizes it before any late response can activate it.
